# Checklist for Procurement of Goods as per General Financial Rules (GFR) norms/ Revision of financial powers by BoG.
This section discusses some general rules that govern purchases from
IIT Bombay projects and grants.

::: {.review}
## Scientific equipment and consumables for research (from July 2025)

The limits in this section apply only to scientific equipment and
consumables bought for research purposes. They follow the Department of
Expenditure [OM No. F.20/42/2021-PPD dated
05.06.2025](http://internal.iitb.ac.in/imcwork/csinfo/specialprov.pdf)
and an [amendment](http://internal.iitb.ac.in/imcwork/csinfo/miiupdated.pdf)
to the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, 2017
(both links open on the campus network only), which
raised the purchase value exempted from Make in India provisions from
₹5 lakhs to ₹50 lakhs for such purchases. Routine (non-research)
purchases continue to follow the existing rules in the sections below.

- *Up to ₹2 lakhs:* purchase directly, without obtaining quotations.
- *Above ₹2 lakhs and up to ₹25 lakhs:* send enquiries to at least 3
  vendors by email, obtain quotations and review compliance
  requirements, then issue the purchase order.
- *Above ₹25 lakhs and up to ₹50 lakhs:* a Limited Tender Enquiry is
  floated on the SRM portal for at least 15 days. GTE approval is not
  required even if the local content is below 20%.
- *Above ₹50 lakhs and up to ₹1 crore:* a Limited Tender Enquiry (where
  known sources of supply are available domestically, as declared by the
  indentor) or an Open Tender Enquiry (where they are not), floated on
  the SRM portal for at least 15 days.
- *Above ₹1 crore:* an open tender on the SRM portal for at least 21
  days, irrespective of the source of supply.
- *Single Tender Enquiry:* up to ₹25 lakhs, floated for 7 days through
  RFQ (offline) or SRM; above ₹25 lakhs, floated on SRM for at least 15
  days. Local content declaration is mandatory above ₹50 lakhs, and GTE
  approval must be obtained if the local content is below 20%.

Other conditions:

- The indentor/PI furnishes a declaration that the items are for
  research purposes, including a statement of compliance with public
  procurement guidelines ([declaration
  template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TVszixfTINbSx7w10DqQ9DDqBH4Lp8Vn/edit)).
- The Director is the competent authority to approve GTE proposals for
  scientific equipment and consumables for research.
- Purchases up to ₹10 lakhs are done at department level. Above ₹10
  lakhs and up to ₹25 lakhs, the purchase is processed at department
  level but the purchase order is issued by MMD after scrutiny by
  Internal Audit.
- Non-GeM procurement is permitted and the GeM Availability Report
  (GeMARPTS) is not required. The indentor may still choose to buy
  through GeM.
- All purchase orders for imports continue to be issued by MMD,
  irrespective of value.

*Source:* email from the Deputy Registrar (MMD) to faculty-notices,
25.07.2025, "Revised purchase process for procurement of scientific
equipment and consumables" (supersedes the email of 07.07.2025).
[Summary of research vs routine purchase
provisions](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1r7x-hsbKa5TDsCqWXruosfJ9Dj5aJiV0/view?usp=sharing)
· [document linked as "ASC Instructions" in the email (titled "Special
Provisions for Procurement of Scientific Equipment &
Consumables")](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1prQ-QWBp6IOGDQ_vY1Y56ianbhXNdEtM/view?usp=sharing)
:::

[The sections below apply to routine (non-research) purchases.]{.review}

## Up to Rs. 1 lakh
Direct market purchase is allowed for items up to Rs. 1 lakh. The
receipt and proof of payment needs to be given along with Dead Stock
Register Entry. Note that Purchase committee is not required for the
Item is priced below Rs. 1 lakh and a direct market purchase is used.

## Above Rs. 1 lakh and up to Rs. 10 lakhs

- A three-member purchase committee to be approved by Head of the Department.
- The committee shall survey the market to ascertain the reasonableness of the rate, quality, and specification. Identify the appropriate supplier and issue a certificate to that effect (GFR 155). If the procurement value is above Rs. 5 lakhs Local Content Declaration is to be obtained from the vendors. Global Tender Enquiry (GTE) approval is mandatory if the Local Content is less than 20%.
- Create a PR for the item to be procured with approximate value.
- If the item is available on Government e-Marketplace (GeM) (https://gem.gov.in/), then a minimum of three quotations from GeM to be obtained and the item should be bought on GeM. One can directly compare three different Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) products for that item - a comparative statement is generated automatically and the least priced item can be bought on GeM.
- In case an item is not available on GeM:
  - Generate a non-availability certificate on GeM. This report should be dated before any quotation dates.
  - Obtain a minimum of 3 original quotations. This is mandatory and the quotations should be dated after the Non-Availability Report
  - Quotations to be signed by all the committee members.
  - Technical/Financial Comparison between the 3 (or more) quotations to be attached.
  - Goods Receipt Note to be attached
  - Dead Stock Register Entry to be made.
  - Competent Authority approval if less than 3 quotations received.
  - Any Other Document required.

::: {.review}
**Updates from 2025–26 circulars (purchases up to ₹10 lakhs)**

- *Purchase committee:* for routine purchases above ₹1 lakh and up to
  ₹10 lakhs (and for research equipment and consumables above ₹2 lakhs
  and up to ₹25 lakhs), the purchase committee is the indentor/PI and
  two members from the same department, approved by the HOD. If the
  indentor is also the approving authority, the formation of the
  committee must be approved by the competent authority one level
  above. The committee's recommendation is mandatory for any amendment
  to the terms and conditions of a purchase order. Where the special
  provisions for research purchases are used, the PI/indentor submits
  a declaration on the nature of the purchase. (*Source:* [Circular
  No. REG/S-7/2025 dated 10.07.2025, Guidelines for the formation of
  the Purchase Committee](https://bighome.iitb.ac.in/index.php/s/MEbqJYPMKfr9SCR).)
- *GeM is mandatory* for all items available on GeM (GFR 149). MMD's
  [Standard Operating Procedure for
  exceptions](http://internal.iitb.ac.in/imcwork/csinfo/gem.pdf)
  (campus network only) applies only to
  exceptional cases, strictly under exigencies. (*Source:* email from
  the Deputy Registrar (MMD) to faculty-notices, 28.04.2025.)
- *Order of steps for a GeM purchase:* (1) create and approve the PR in
  ERP; (2) source the item on GeM (Direct Market/Bid/Custom Bid/BOQ);
  (3) evaluate bids and prepare the Technical Committee Report
  (offline); (4) accept or disqualify technical bids on GeM; (5) open
  the commercial bid on GeM and identify the L1 bidder; (6) prepare the
  Purchase Committee Report (offline) and create the Demand on GeM; (7)
  create the DPO in ERP against the pre-approved GeM PR, attaching the
  GeM documents; (8) obtain all approvals in ERP; (9) create the final
  PO in ERP; (10) execute the contract on GeM. Do not process a GeM
  contract first and create the PO only at payment time. (*Source:*
  email from the Deputy Registrar (MMD) to faculty-notices, 07.01.2025;
  [GeM procure-to-pay process
  document](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k2T889j5vx9ofTNeKL4NqoKsJMI7fozk/view?usp=sharing).)
- *Payment details on GeM:* secondary buyers must update payment
  details against GeM orders immediately (using the Bulk Payment
  Utility). Non-compliance can lead to suspension of the buyer ID or
  deactivation of IIT Bombay's nodal account. (*Source:* email from the
  Deputy Registrar (MMD) to faculty-notices, 22.04.2026.)
- *No brand names in specifications:* procurement documents must not
  name specific brands, makes or trade names (GFR 144(i)(b); Clause
  10(e) of the PPP-MII Order 2017 as amended on 19.07.2024).
  Specifications should be neutral, reasonable and performance-based.
  (*Source:* email from the Dean (R&D) and Associate Dean (R&D) to
  faculty-notices, 25.04.2025.)
- *ERP:* for research purchases, select the ZSCI document type when
  creating the PR; an "Additional Text" field (up to 500 characters)
  holds the justification and appears on the GFR printout. (*Source:*
  email from the Head, Application Software Centre, to faculty-notices,
  24.07.2026.)
- *Devices for professional use from donation projects (Dean (ACR)):*
  attach a scanned, signed "Undertaking" to the PR in ERP. (*Source:*
  email from the Office of the Dean (ACR) to faculty-notices,
  21.08.2025.)
:::
